finding: Strong evidence of two knees in one study, supported by explicit left/right source sections, repeated acquisitions and two independent27-panel native anatomy/orientation reviews.
decision: Retain whole-study report supervision fully masked for current single-knee training. Preserve raw source, images and official gold unchanged. Any later derived side-specific unit requires a separately validated series-to-side/report binding and parent-patient leakage grouping; no arbitrary selection, label cloning or automatic virtual split.
limitations: Anatomical side inference assumes DICOM orientation is correct and upstream pixels were not silently mirrored. Missing laterality is never treated as right without anatomy/orientation evidence.
Full source-byte hashes were checked by the inspected native download script; retained endpoint prefix digests remain prefix-only, independently checked against full-record metadata and identity.
No disease diagnoses or gold values inferred from these visual samples. One pseudonymous patient ID does not prove real-world identity.
Current official report copy already contains both sides; no claim that local recovery created this aggregation.
